Senses.Explanation: The southern bough is the records’ shortened name for the Southern Bough dream and its vanished dream-world. The ant-kingdom element is stated inside the corpus: Zhean Jingfan's verse says “the Southern Bough ant-hole—enter the dream and travel” (南柯蟻穴，入夢來遊). Baichi Yuan calls his hall activity “all one Southern Bough dream,” while Huqiu Shaolong speaks of getting free of it and seeing human affairs as empty. The name also enters encounter grammar without a story retelling. In Yunmen Wenyan's probing section, after calling an answer a dream, the record supplies several substitute responses, including the bare word “Southern Bough.” Dayu Shouzhi asks what his own dream-talk dreamed and follows with “Southern Bough, ten watches.” The Zen deviation is this compression and reuse: a literary dream-name becomes a one-word substitute response, the named content of Dayu Shouzhi's dream-talk, and a repeated line in hall addresses and case verses.

An exposed failure is a defect made visible in an answer, exchange, action, or speaker's handling of a case. In Chinese Chan records the compound is a recurrent verdict of failure on an exchange, statement, answer, or speaker. The corpus has attested. It records the constructions 'incur a failure' (納敗闕, attested), 'a whole episode of failure' (一場敗闕, attested), and 'the place of the failure' (敗闕處, attested). In one direct exchange an unnamed questioner asks, 'What failure do I have?' and receives the answer 'Wrong.' Elsewhere Dahui quotes Linji calling an old man's response 'a failure today,' then answers the question 'Where is his failure?' with 'The road is far and the night is long; stop carrying a torch, everyone, and blow it out while walking in the dark.' Yuan Cheng is asked how to have no failure and replies, 'Eat three meals.' A later comment can apply the verdict to both parties while also calling both adept: 'As failures, both are failures; as adepts, both are adepts.' These records leave the verdict attached to the cited exchange rather than supplying one universal defect that the word always names.
Senses.Note: The word carries a military register: 'rout' (敗) plus 'breach' (闕) becomes a verdict that an exchange has failed, as in 'a whole episode of failure' (一場敗闕) and 'incur a failure' (納敗闕). All seven required definition formulas were searched; none produced a lexical definition. The entry therefore foregrounds the direct 'what failure?' exchange, the 'where is the failure?' retrospective, verdict uses, and the corpus's own two-party contrast. The rare 'no failure' construction (無敗闕) has one hit in one text. Exact actors are named on every retained occurrence except the source-anonymous questioning monk, whose reviewed exception record preserves all six attribution rungs.
